children: GE Aerospace CEO Larry Culp says demand continues to be solid across the business, despite operating in a dynamic environment. The jet engine maker says 3Q orders increased 49%, led by the company's commercial-engines and services segment, with orders up 58% in that unit. "We continue to see strength in commercial services, with orders up 23% in the third quarter and 30% year to date," Culp says on a call with analysts. "Combined with our backlog of over $170 billion, we're well positioned to close out 2026 and now expect low double digit services growth in 2027." GE Aerospace is off 3% premarket. (connor.hart@wsj.com)
